reconstructed_words.reasoning: καὶ εἶπεν is the standard LXX rendering of וַיֹּאמֶר throughout the Pentateuch, representing one of the most consistent translation equivalences in Exodus. The waw-consecutive qal imperfect of אמר is rendered by the Greek aorist indicative with conjunction. No deviation from MT is detectable.

ὁ θεός is the consistent LXX rendering of אֱלֹהִים throughout the Pentateuch. The definite article in Greek reflects the anaphoric use of the noun in context. The MT reads אֱלֹהִים here without the divine name YHWH, which the LXX faithfully reflects.

πάλιν renders עֹוד in a temporal/sequential sense meaning 'again' or 'still/furthermore.' This is an established LXX equivalent for עֹוד when it introduces a repeated divine speech act; see Gen 8:10, 8:12 and elsewhere in LXX Exodus. The MT reads עֹוד in exactly this position.

alternatives.note: Theoretically possible but not supported by translation pattern here; עֹוד is the standard lexical basis for πάλιν.

reconstructed_words.reasoning: πρός + accusative consistently renders אֶל in LXX Exodus speech formulae. The proper name Μωυσῆν reflects מֹשֶׁה with standard Greek nominal adaptation. No divergence from MT is indicated.

οὕτως ἐρεῖς is the standard rendering of the messenger formula כֹּה תֹאמַר; οὕτως renders כֹּה and ἐρεῖς renders the qal imperfect of אמר. This phrase appears identically in Ex 3:14 and throughout prophetic and legal formulae in the LXX. Full agreement with MT.

τοῖς υἱοῖς Ισραηλ reflects בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל with consistent lexical equivalence: υἱοί = בְּנֵי, Ισραηλ = יִשְׂרָאֵל. The preposition אֶל is absorbed into the dative construction in Greek. The MT is exactly reproduced.

κύριος is the standard LXX surrogate for the Tetragrammaton throughout the Pentateuch; this is Tov's well-documented translator convention. The Vorlage certainly had יְהוָה here as in the MT, and the translator rendered it by κύριος per standard practice without any alternate Hebrew base.

ὁ θεός renders the construct אֱלֹהֵי, τῶν πατέρων renders אֲבֹתֵי, and ὑμῶν renders the second-person plural suffix כֶם. This is a completely regular rendering of the construct chain. The MT and Vorlage are identical.
θεός renders the construct אֱלֹהֵי, and Αβρααμ is the standard Greek transliteration of אַבְרָהָם. The construct chain is faithfully rendered. Full agreement with MT.

καί renders the conjunction ו, θεός renders אֱלֹהֵי in construct, and Ισαακ is the standard transliteration of יִצְחָק. The MT has the conjunction before אֱלֹהֵי יִצְחָק, and the LXX reflects this exactly.

Identical analysis to the preceding entry: καί = ו, θεός = אֱלֹהֵי in construct, Ιακωβ = יַעֲקֹב. The tripartite patriarchal formula is rendered consistently across all three members, in full agreement with MT.

ἀπέσταλκεν renders שָׁלַח (piel/qal perfect 3ms), με renders the first-person object suffix נִי, and πρὸς ὑμᾶς renders אֲלֵיכֶם. The Greek perfect ἀπέσταλκεν for the Hebrew perfect שְׁלָחַנִי is a standard rendering choice in LXX Exodus. Full agreement with MT.

τοῦτο renders זֶה, μού ἐστιν renders the pronominal suffix י on שְׁמִי (with ἐστιν as a Greek copula addition reflecting the nominal clause), ὄνομα renders שֵׁם, and αἰώνιον renders לְעֹלָם. The LXX translator renders the adverbial לְעֹלָם as an attributive adjective αἰώνιον, a standard Greek idiom that does not indicate a divergent Vorlage. Full agreement with MT.

μνημόσυνον renders זִכְרִי (a standard equivalence; cf. Ex 17:14; Ps 9:6 LXX), and γενεῶν γενεαῖς renders לְדֹר דֹּר. Notably, the demonstrative pronoun זֶה is not rendered explicitly; the Greek phrase καὶ μνημόσυνον functions as an appositive nominal without an expressed demonstrative. The most significant divergence is γενεῶν γενεαῖς (genitive + dative) for לְדֹר דֹּר, which is an unusual rendering: the MT has the phrase meaning 'to generation and generation' (= 'for all generations'), but the Greek γενεῶν γενεαῖς ('of generations, to generations') uses two different cases, suggesting the translator may have read a slightly expanded or repointed form, possibly לְדֹרֵי דֹרֹת or simply interpreted the idiom dynamically. This is possibly a Greek stylistic rendering rather than a different Vorlage.

alternatives.note: An expanded form attested elsewhere in the HB (e.g., Isa 51:8) could explain γενεῶν γενεαῖς, though this is speculative without DSS support.
The MT reading itself, with the unusual double-case Greek rendering being an idiomatic translator choice rather than a divergent Vorlage.

summary_technical: The LXX of Exodus 3:15 reflects a Vorlage substantially identical to the MT across all major elements, with consistent translation equivalences that conform to well-documented LXX Exodus patterns (κύριος = יְהוָה, ἀπέσταλκεν = שָׁלַח, etc.). The only notable point of divergence from a purely mechanical rendering is γενεῶν γενεαῖς for לְדֹר דֹּר, where the translator employs two distinct Greek cases (genitive + dative) rather than a simple prepositional phrase, possibly reflecting an idiomatic or interpretive rendering rather than a different Hebrew text. No DSS fragments (e.g., from 4QpaleoExod-m or 4QExod-b) are currently known to attest a reading divergent from MT at this specific verse.
summary_plain: The Greek translation of Exodus 3:15 closely follows the same Hebrew text we have in the traditional Bible (the Masoretic Text), with only minor differences in style that reflect how the Greek translator chose to express Hebrew idioms, not a different underlying Hebrew original.

bibcrit_assessment.title: LXX γενεῶν γενεαῖς: Idiomatic or Variant Vorlage?
bibcrit_assessment.reasoning: The most philologically significant point in this verse is the rendering of לְדֹר דֹּר as γενεῶν γενεαῖς, using genitive and dative where a single prepositional phrase would be expected. While this could reflect a Vorlage with לְדֹרֵי דֹרֹת (attested in late Biblical Hebrew; cf. Isa 51:8; Ps 72:5), the evidence for this is purely circumstantial and speculative; it is more parsimonious to attribute the double case to the translator's Greek literary sensibility, distributing the repeated Hebrew term across two syntactic functions to produce a more elegant Greek phrase. The omission of an explicit Greek equivalent for the second זֶה is similarly best explained as the translator's preference for paratactic flow rather than evidence for its absence in the Vorlage.
bibcrit_assessment.plain: The most interesting translation choice in this verse is how the Greek handles the Hebrew phrase 'to generation and generation' using two different grammatical cases, which may simply be a stylistic choice by the translator rather than evidence that he had a different Hebrew text in front of him.

_validation.confidence_note: The analysis is broadly sound on translation equivalences but contains a significant lexical error (πάλιν) and some overstated claims about translator conventions.

flagged_claims.claim: πάλιν renders עֹוד in a temporal/sequential sense
flagged_claims.reason: The actual LXX of Exodus 3:15 does not contain πάλιν. The Greek text reads καὶ εἶπεν ὁ θεὸς πάλιν πρὸς Μωυσῆν in some editions, but more importantly, πάλιν as a rendering of עֹוד needs verification—the standard LXX Exodus 3:15 word order and contents should be checked against Rahlfs/Göttingen. The reconstruction itself may be misaligned with the actual LXX text.

flagged_claims.claim: μνημόσυνον renders זִכְרִי ... cf. Ex 17:14; Ps 9:6 LXX
flagged_claims.reason: While μνημόσυνον does render זֵכֶר/זִכָּרוֹן in LXX, the specific cross-references should be verified; Ps 9:6 LXX citation in particular needs checking as the verse numbering and content vary.

flagged_claims.claim: An expanded form attested elsewhere in the HB (e.g., Isa 51:8) could explain γενεῶν γενεαῖς
flagged_claims.reason: Isa 51:8 reads לְדוֹר דּוֹרִים, not לְדֹרֵי דֹרֹת; the cited parallel does not actually support the proposed reconstruction.

flagged_claims.claim: this is Tov's well-documented translator convention
flagged_claims.reason: Attribution of the κύριος=YHWH convention specifically to Tov is imprecise; this is a general scholarly observation, and whether the original LXX used κύριος or preserved the Tetragrammaton (as in some early MSS like P. Fouad 266) is actually debated.

flagged_claims.claim: No DSS fragments (e.g., from 4QpaleoExod-m or 4QExod-b) are currently known to attest a reading divergent from MT at this specific verse
flagged_claims.reason: This claim requires verification against DJD volumes; absence of evidence is being asserted without explicit citation, and 4QExod-b/4QpaleoExod-m coverage of Ex 3:15 should be confirmed.

flagged_claims.claim: The Greek perfect ἀπέσταλκεν for the Hebrew perfect שְׁלָחַנִי is a standard rendering choice in LXX Exodus
flagged_claims.reason: Hebrew perfect is more typically rendered by Greek aorist; the Greek perfect here may actually be marked/unusual rather than standard, and this should be verified.
